exclude: not map data: the unpacker runs on past the 1024-byte tile layer until its input count runs out, decoding the next entry's packed bytes with this entry's table; nothing reads them and the map is never written back from here

comments.text: Class layer, rows 0-31 of 32x32: a nibble a square, even column in the high nibble (map_class_at $0953). Squares by class: 0: 275, 1: 88, 2: 16, 10: 6, 11: 639.

Number layer, rows 0-31: one byte a square, the entry of its class's list that holds the square's record (map_number_row $098E, action_record $09B8). 1 squares of classes without a handler (0, 7, 13, 14) have a non-zero number, which nothing uses.

The number of square (9, 29). Game `$B4F0` `bit $39A9` names it because of the BIT-skip idiom: the operand's bytes are the `lda #$39` the code enters at `$B4F1`. On choose_attack's path through the LDA #$50 at $B4EE (api_is_ranged_class at $B4E4 returning carry clear and weapon_rounds at $B4E9 returning 0) the BIT does execute and read this byte, but its flags are replaced before anything tests them (N and Z by LDA #$92 at $1DC4, V by the ADC at $28E5, both on game_msg's path), so its value never matters.

Map code entry 0 (action 0): gives the party's first member a disease: select_member with A = 1 ($0335), then sets bit n of the character's disease byte +$28, n = the square's record byte +3, through the mask table at $3C51 (the same routine as map 5's at $3C9E). The bits are module 0's diseases (bit 2 Bug byte, 4 Desert dust, 5 Rabies); any of them stops natural healing (game $B854), and bits 4 and 5 also cost CON over time (game $B7A6, $B816). Returns carry clear.
